articles.title_zh: Taylor Swift Shares Rare Glimpse at Her and Travis Kelce's Road Trip to Cleveland
articles.content_orig:
Taylor Swift knew it, she knew you would want an inside look at her romance.
The "Patient Zero" singer offered a rare glimpse at a recent road trip she took with Travis Kelce to his Ohio hometown as part of the lyric video for her new song "Cleveland!"
In one clip from the visuals posted to her YouTube Sept. 25 , Swift filmed Kelce—who she tied the knot with in July—as he drove his car down the freeway. When he realized he was being filmed, the Kansas City Chief's player—who kept it casual for the trip in a blue striped shirt, black baseball hat and gold chain necklace—gave a wide smile.
Following the sweet moment, the camera then panned to a highway sign that revealed the pair were, indeed, headed towards downtown Cleveland before turning back to Swift, who looked equally excited to arrive at their destination while sitting in the passenger seat.
And that's not the only footage that will make you feel so high school about their memorable excursion. In several other snippets, Swift provided a peek at a cute shopping strip they perused, a tree-lined neighborhood they cruised down and their return to Cleveland Heights High School, which Kelce attended.
Of course, the lyrics of "Cleveland!"—which arrived on Sept. 25 as part of a four-track deluxe edition of her 2025 album The Life of a Showgirl, called The Encore —also revealed some intimacies about Swift and Kelce, both 36.
On the song, Swift sings about how she's able to block out the noise from her critics because she's finally found the "love of my life." And in addition to making the sweet declaration, she also reveals an adorable pet name that Kelce calls her, singing, "He says I look like an angel."
"He already took me to Cleveland / And showed me The Heights, so hate all you like,” the lyrics read. "This is the love of my life."
For more Easter eggs in The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, keep reading.
Back in 2024, the Los Angeles Times called Taylor Swift "patient zero for emotional contagion," which may have inspired her lyrics from this single off Life of a Showgirl: The Encore , out Sept. 25, 2026.
But it turns out "Patient Zero"—which features Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell in the music video—is about Taylor bonding with a woman over a mutual ex, beginning with, "If you wanna party with somebody who might know / About the devil on his shoulder under his halo / When the toxins take their hold, you'd rather die than let it go / But if you’re sick of him, I got you, I was patient zero."
If an ex having a halo (or lack thereof) sounds familiar, she also touched on that theme in "I Can Fix Him (No Really I Can)" from Tortured Poets , which seemingly alluded to her ex Matty Healy . Taylor sang at the time, "He had a halo of the highest grade/ He just hadn't met me yet."
Now that Taylor is happily married, she is imparting wisdom on her ex's new partner in "Patient Zero."
"Take it from somebody who lost his games but won the race / Take it from someone who said all of this to his face," she says. "Someone who knows she's more than just the chase / Someone who had him and walked away."
So, who could she be singing about? It could have been inspired by her girls' night out with Sophie Turner shortly after the actress' 2023 split with Joe Jonas , who Taylor dated in 2008. (He is also believed to have inspired Fearless ' "Forever & Always" and "Mr. Perfectly Fine.")
The love song is a clear nod to her husband Travis Kelce 's roots as a native of Cleveland Heights, Ohio. The pair have already spent time there, as Travis reportedly purchased a $5.35 million lakefront property in the area in March 2026.
Similar to Tortured Poet 's "But Daddy I Love Him," Taylor is clapping back at anyone questioning their relationship in "Cleveland!"
"And now I guess there's / Something we all can agree on / But my baby likes what he likes," she sings. "He already took me to Cleveland / And showed me The Heights, so hate all you like / This is the love of my life."
Beyond defending their romance, Taylor also fires back at critics of her career and fashion sense by quoting some frequent disses she's heard.
"She's not as hot as she was, but she was only a four / She was never a girls' girl, she was just a— / And with all of that money, why's she dressed like trash? / When she smiles, it's annoying, and have you seen her / Stumbling clumsily? / Would you even call that dancing?"
Forget the lavender haze. Instead, "Pink Clouding" expresses regret over how Taylor handled a past breakup: "Years later, I still wonder how to tell you sorry / I didn't wanna let you down / So I left you up there on a, pink cloud."
The self-reflection has fans speculating that she could be writing about Tom Hiddleston (post-"Getaway Car") or Taylor Lautner (post-"Back to December"), who she's been on good terms with in recent years.
However, she also refers to meeting her lover during a challenging time in her life, possibly alluding to her ex Joe Alwyn , who she grew close with during her reputation era.
"Ripped all my orchids from the vine / You met me at a cursed time / I told you I was fine," she sings, reminiscent of "I once was poison ivy, but now, I'm your daisy" from 2017's "Don't Blame Me."
During her relationship with Joe, she frequently expressed worry about thrusting him into a life of fame and scrutiny (like in folklore 's "Peace") and "Pink Clouding" plays on similar themes.
"I hope / You realized my kind of trouble wasn't worth it," the lyrics read. "And the way I treated you, you never deserved it / And I swear to God, to this day / I wake up scared that I left scars on a good person."
Taylor sings about knowing hindsight is 20/20 when it comes to love, writing about "missing all the best parts" of a past relationship: "You never knew that it was Babylon 'til it was gone."
She previously mentioned the Gardens of Babylon—one of the Seven Wonders of the World, located in modern day Iraq—in her 2020 evermore song "Cowboy like Me," which features the lines, "Now you hang from my lips / Like the Gardens of Babylon / With your boots beneath my bed / Forever is the sweetest con."
Of course, she's since found that forever with Travis—who got down on one knee in (you guessed it) an enchanting garden in their Kansas City backyard.
The opening song on Taylor's The Life of a Showgirl references the character Ophelia from William Shakespeare 's Hamlet , who faces a tragic fate.
According to the song's lyrics, Taylor "might've drowned in the melancholy" if she hadn't been saved by her true love.
"I heard you calling / On the megaphone," Taylor sings. "You wanna see me all alone."
The lyrics appear to be a nod to Travis calling Taylor out on his New Heights podcast for not meeting him at her Eras Tour, which is how their romance began.
"I swore loyalty to me, myself and I," the lyrics continue. "Right before you lit my sky up."
Before meeting Travis, Taylor was fresh off a breakup from Matty Healy, having declared herself one of the "independent girlies" in July 2023.
But after Travis went to her concert in Kansas City that same month, sparks began to fly.
Now, Taylor's fiancé is even in on her Easter egg game, teasing "The Fate of Ophelia" lyrics on Instagram back in July. (Had some adventures this offseason," he captioned pics with Taylor, adding, "Kept it [100].")
How does that connect to Taylor's song? Well, as the lyrics go, "You dug me out of my grave and saved my heart from the fate of Ophelia / Keep it one hundred."
Taylor gives a nod to another famous showgirl, the late Elizabeth Taylor , in the second song on the album, even naming Elizabeth's favorite places, Paris' Plaza Athénée as well as Los Angeles' Musso & Frank's.
In the lyrics, Taylor also draws parallels between her and the Cleopatra actress. Like Taylor today, Elizabeth often made headlines for everything from her love life to her dazzling outfits.
But, as Taylor notes in her song, "Oftentimes it doesn't feel so glamorous to be me."

Marcus Mariota will be the Commanders’ starting quarterback for whatever games Jayden Daniels misses with his left elbow injury. And Mariota and Daniels will both be team captains for the rest of the season.
Commanders coach Dan Quinn announced on Friday that the five Commanders who were chosen as team captains before the season got together and decided they want Mariota to be a captain, not just while he’s the starting quarterback but also when he returns to the No. 2 job when Daniels returns.
“I thought it was such a cool thing: The captains huddled up with me earlier in week and said, ‘We’d like to make Marcus our sixth captain,’” Quinn said. “I thought, What a great tribute of brotherhood of those guys asking. They were all as on board as you could imagine. I thought it was awesome, too. What a great example of teammate and leadership.”
The Commanders say Mariota’s status as captain for the rest of the season is not an indication that he’ll be starting for long, as the team expects Daniels to be back soon. But even if Mariota spends most of the season on the bench, he’ll have the captain’s C on his jersey.
In addition to Mariota and Daniels, the Commanders’ captains are wide receiver Terry McLaurin, linebacker Frankie Luvu, safety Jeremy Reaves and punter Tress Way.

articles.title_zh: Hong Kong designer’s slow fashion label puts Chinese ethnic artisans first
articles.content_orig:
Kinyan Lam’s eponymous brand champions natural materials, dyeing and embroidery from China’s Dong ethnic minority group
Hong Kong designer Kinyan Lam’s autumn/winter 2026 collection, Grounded, is more than a seasonal drop. It sets a clear vision for the future of his eponymous brand: that slowing down is the only way forward.
“I heard a saying that plants and trees have two ways of growing: they explode into the world, but their roots continue to dig deep into the soil,” says Lam, who is in his thirties. “Right now, I am just a small tree, and I want to grow my roots deeper so I can grow into a big tree. This is a moment for our brand to become really grounded.”
After studying at the Hong Kong Design Institute (HKDI), Lam went on to earn a master’s degree at the London College of Fashion from 2019 to 2020. He later returned to Hong Kong to teach at his alma mater, where he developed a passion for textiles and natural dyeing. In 2021, he founded Genau Studio, which offers garment-dyeing services and workshops focused on natural dyes.
Lam credits his love for nature to his childhood growing up in a small village in China’s Guangdong province, before he moved to Hong Kong aged 10.

articles.title_orig: Damning Elon Musk Film Hit With Shocking Censorship
articles.title_zh: Damning Elon Musk Film Hit With Shocking Censorship
articles.content_orig:
Elon Musk’s extraordinary power is making it remarkably difficult to advertise a documentary about just how powerful Elon Musk has become.
YouTube, TikTok, Instagram, Facebook owner Meta, and, predictably, Musk’s own platform X have all refused to run paid advertisements for Academy Award-winning filmmaker Alex Gibney’s new four-hour documentary Musk , according to The Hollywood Reporter .
The film’s independent distributor, Bleecker Street, has been told by several platforms that the content violates their bans on “political content,” even though it promotes a movie trailer—not a candidate or political campaign.
YouTube, TikTok, and Meta have reportedly blocked Bleecker Street’s ads, claiming the trailer breaches their ban on political ads. The film contains scenes from political rallies, but is not itself a political advertisement. Instagram has not yet said why it rejected the ad.
Bleecker Street has appealed the platforms’ decisions. Meta has already rejected the appeal , while TikTok and YouTube are still weighing whether to allow the ads, according to The Hollywood Reporter.
X is reportedly refusing to communicate with Bleecker Street, and has so far refused to accept advertising for any of its upcoming films.
Gibney’s documentary “depicts the world’s richest man as petty, narcissistic, megalomaniacal, cruel, [and] detached from humans at a personal level (including various ex-partners and many of his children),” according to Deadline’s Matthew Carey .
The Tesla and SpaceX CEO slammed the film, which premiered at the Venice International Film Festival earlier this month, as a “ hit piece ,” and has threatened legal action.
The social media wall now helping to shield Musk underscores a key point in the film: the tech mogul is so alarmingly wealthy and powerful that he wields enormous influence over what the public sees and learns.
“I do worry about the storm clouds on the horizon ,” Gibney admitted while promoting the film in Venice. He said he encountered a “ tremendous sense of fear ” among his Musk sources. “Many, many, many, many” people refused to speak out, he noted.
Universal is releasing the film overseas after reversing a decision to drop it following a public outcry.
The Daily Beast has reached out to Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Instagram, and X for comment.
Musk will arrive in select theaters in New York and Los Angeles on Oct. 9, then roll out nationwide one week later.

articles.title_orig: White House blocks CNN from trip on Air Force One
articles.title_zh: White House blocks CNN from trip on Air Force One
articles.content_orig:
Outlet had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, network said Friday
The White House has blocked CNN from traveling aboard Air Force One on Saturday, impeding its TV press pool duties in the latest escalation of the administration’s battle with the news media.
CNN had been scheduled to fly with Donald Trump to Tennessee for a college football game, the network said on Friday . The White House confirmed CNN’s exclusion when it did not list the network on guidance sent to the press corps regarding Trump’s schedule for Saturday.
CNN’s exclusion from Air Force One was first reported by the Washington Post . The White House did not immediately return the Guardian’s request for comment.
The incident comes a week after Trump, a vocal critic of what he deems the “fake news media”, revoked White House access for CNN, MS Now and Politico, citing unfavorable reports about his presidency.
“Media Outlets shouldn’t be able to constantly write or report FICTION and LIES,” Trump wrote then on Truth Social, vowing that similar action would be taken against other outlets.
The extraordinary move prompted swift backlash from the White House press pool, who suspended their video coverage of Trump in protest.
The press pool is a rotating group of journalists charged with covering presidential travel and disseminating written and multimedia reports to news outlets that may not be present at a given White House event. Since the beginning of Trump’s second administration in 2025, the White House has decided which outlets cover the president via the pool each day, a task previously coordinated by the White House Correspondents’ Association.
In a joint statement Monday, the White House television pool said: “The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government. No administration should restrict a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
In a subsequent lawsuit , CNN, MS Now and Politico argued the White House ban was a violation of the first amendment.
Meanwhile, the Department of Justice’s attorneys suggested the ban was in the interest of national security, pointing at media reports involving “sensitive” and “classified” information.
The US district judge Timothy Kelly sided with the outlets, ordering the Trump administration to restore their White House access.
CNN, MS Now and Politico’s journalists sought to enter the White House on Thursday morning, but were not granted entry until midday.
Hours later, CNN’s editorial team along with an MS Now reporter were blocked from covering the state dinner commemorating Chinese president Xi Jinping’s visit.
